purpose: Document a possible local Apple Silicon port and its acceptance tests. This profile is not the recommended scientific run and has not been executed.

device.host: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB unified memory
device.availability_evidence: Existing tiny-model and tensor diagnostics report MPS available in a normal Terminal process; the restricted command sandbox cannot access Metal. Full-model training has not been tested.
device.estimate_basis: Approximately 1.2 billion parameters at 4 bytes each for FP32 weights, 4 bytes for gradients, and 8 bytes for two FP32 Adam moments; excludes activations, temporary buffers, allocator overhead, and macOS memory.

training_adaptations.distributed_launcher: single-process Python; no Accelerate multi-GPU or DeepSpeed ZeRO-3
deviations_from_upstream: FP32 in place of upstream BF16.
PyTorch SDPA in place of flash_attention_2.
torch AdamW in place of bitsandbytes paged_adamw_32bit; the paged optimizer is not part of the current Apple Metal support matrix.
One MPS process in place of two CUDA processes and DeepSpeed ZeRO-3.
Microbatch 1 with accumulation 32 to preserve a nominal global batch of 32; order, sampler behavior, kernel numerics, and throughput will still differ from distributed CUDA.

mathematical_equivalence_acceptance_test.reference: Pinned OpenUnlearning GradDiff implementation with fixed token IDs, attention masks, labels, and the same tiny causal model weights.
tests: Compare forget NLL, retain NLL, combined GradDiff scalar loss, and all parameter gradients between the official expression and the MPS adapter on a tiny model.

Compare one and multiple optimizer updates from identical initial weights and fixed gradients; compare paged AdamW32bit versus torch AdamW in a CUDA preflight, then compare MPS torch AdamW versus CPU torch AdamW.
Verify the same chat template, label masking, padding masks, per-token reduction, retain sampling distribution, and effective batch aggregation before any model-sized run.
mathematical_equivalence_acceptance_test.acceptance_rule: All fixed-batch loss, gradient, and update comparisons must pass before considering a full-model MPS pilot. Passing small-model tests establishes objective/update agreement only; it does not establish full-model fit, runtime, deterministic kernels, or benchmark equivalence.
mathematical_equivalence_acceptance_test.execution_status: No code for these equivalence checks has been run in this task.

resource_and_claim_limits.full_model_peak_memory: unknown; no full-model MPS training measurement exists
